Variants.Content: Ashford is an important town in the southwest of the Reach, famous for the Ashford family and the local jousting tradition. Settled between rivers, roads, and fertile fields, towns could host caravans, farmers, knights, and fairgoers; the honor of the jousting ground thus existed alongside the bustle of the marketplace. The tournament in the Reach is not just about personal reputation. It brings accommodation, horses, iron, wine and taxes, and also allows different lords to exchange marriage contracts and news in a short period of peace. The normal situation in Cen Shu Tan is still food, cloth and seasonal work, rather than the birth of heroes every year.
Entry Ashford Local families also relied on grain, wine, orchards, pastures, and markets along the Mander River; if any road, well, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Ashford They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the Reach; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Ashford If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Those who repair the ash beach are familiar with the stone walls, wooden beams, iron doors, tombs, and the seams left by generations of repairs. Those who comfort the families of the deceased are familiar with the memories of family status left in the days of the Seven Gods, the Legend of Chivalry, and the Gardener King. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Ashford They care about grain, wine, orchards, pastures and markets along the Mander River. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
